eventMetadata.context_description: Iowa's star running back Kaleb Johnson is officially out for the Black Friday clash at Kinnick Stadium, severely hampering the Hawkeyes' already struggling ground attack that ranks near the bottom nationally in yards per carry. This shifts leverage to Nebraska's stout run defense, which has limited opponents to under 100 rushing yards in four of their last six games. The Cornhuskers enter with freshman QB Dylan Raiola's efficient arm fueling a balanced offense, despite a recent overtime loss to USC snapping a mini-streak. Iowa's elite defense and home-field edge in the rivalry keep it close historically—Nebraska has dropped seven straight—but traders' 60% consensus on the Huskers reflects the Hawkeyes' offensive woes and bowl-motivated urgency for Matt Rhule's squad to hit six wins.
